_about: A frozen retrieval eval set shaped the way BEIR's loader hands one to a scorer -- corpus {id: {title,
text}}, queries {id: text}, qrels {query id: {doc id: grade}} (Thakur et al., NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and
Benchmarks, https://openreview.net/forum?id=wCu6T5xFjeJ). It is one JSON file, not BEIR's three on-disk
files, so it is the shape and not the format. retrieval.py seeds `corpus` onto the test site as Drive
documents, asks `queries` through rag.search.search, and scores what comes back against `qrels`. A grade
is 1 unless stated, and a document not listed is not relevant to that question.
The corpus is the demo site's own seven policy documents, copied verbatim so the check measures the
corpus the product is demonstrated on. Every question and every qrel was written by reading those
documents, not by running a search: several questions deliberately use the vocabulary of a document
that does NOT answer them (q01 says 'travelling' but is answered by the expense policy, q04 and q05 say
'expense' but are answered by the reimbursement policy), because a question whose answer is also its
q13 is the one graded question: the reimbursement policy answers 'by when' outright (2), while the
expense and travel policies each answer part of 'what' (1). Without a graded question nothing would
exercise nDCG's gain term at all -- with one relevant document per question the numerator is the same
1 at every rank -- and one question with three answers is also the only thing here that can tell a
reordering of the top three from a miss.
Ceiling: seven documents and thirteen questions. This size catches a retriever that has broken, been
pointed at the wrong model, or lost its permission filter. It cannot separate two working rankers.

expense-policy.txt.title: Expense policy
expense-policy.txt.text: Expense policy: meals capped at 45 AUD per day.

parental-leave.txt.title: Parental Leave Policy
parental-leave.txt.text:
Parental Leave Policy

Primary carers receive 18 weeks of paid parental leave at full pay.

Secondary carers receive 4 weeks. Leave must commence within 12 months of the birth or adoption.

reimbursement-policy.txt.title: Reimbursement Policy
reimbursement-policy.txt.text:
L2X Technologies Pty Ltd

Reimbursement Policy

Claims must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date.

Page two: approvals above 200 AUD need a manager signature.

remote-work.txt.title: Remote Work Policy
remote-work.txt.text:
Remote Work Policy

Staff may work remotely up to three days per week.

Fully remote arrangements require written approval from a department head and a home office allowance of 600 AUD applies.

security-policy.txt.title: Security Policy
security-policy.txt.text:
Security Policy

Lost or stolen laptops must be reported to the security desk within 4 hours.

The replacement excess for a lost laptop is 250 AUD.

travel-policy.txt.title: Travel policy
travel-policy.txt.text: Travel policy: economy under four hours. Café receipts accepted.

vehicle-policy.txt.title: Vehicle policy
vehicle-policy.txt.text: Vehicle policy: mileage reimbursed at 88 cents per kilometre.

queries.q01: What is the daily limit on meals while I am travelling?
queries.q02: How much paid leave does a primary carer get?
queries.q03: Can a secondary carer take paid leave, and for how long?
queries.q04: How many days after paying for something do I have to file the claim?
queries.q05: Does a large expense claim need someone to sign it off?
queries.q06: How often am I allowed to work from home?
queries.q07: Is there money towards a desk and chair at home?
queries.q08: My laptop was stolen, how quickly must I tell someone?
queries.q09: What do I have to pay myself if a laptop is lost?
queries.q10: Which cabin am I booked in for a two hour flight?
queries.q11: What do I get back per kilometre for driving my own car?
queries.q12: By when must parental leave start after a birth?
queries.q13: What can I claim back after a work trip, and by when?
